title: A coding agent learns Novis by asking the binary, and every adapter that points it there carries no language content of its own
scope:
how an agent writing Novis gets what it needs — the surface it asks, what that surface
answers, and what an install writes into a user's project. It decides nothing about the language,
nothing about `nvs-lsp`, whose audience is an editor rather than a model, and nothing about the
one-file reference, which keeps the job [0089](0089.md) gave it.
dependsOnText:
[0089](0089.md) for the reference pipeline, and `rule:tooling/one-json-several-renderers`
for the shape a fourth consumer joins.
validatedBy:
`tests/conformance/tooling/` — the index resolving member for member against the
registry, and every refusal the primer states proven against the compiler that refuses it.

summary.headline: A coding agent learns Novis by asking the compiler, not by reading the repo
summary.body:
`nvs agent` prints a short primer, searches a one-line-per-member index of the standard library
and shows a card for one member, all generated from the same registry the compiler carries. An
agent reads the primer once and pays a few hundred tokens per lookup, instead of loading a
reference far larger than its context. `nvs agent init` writes one pointer file per coding
harness, and the pointer says where to ask and nothing about the language itself, because a
stated fact is a copy that goes stale the day a member changes.
